instructions: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Cook it in a rice cooker, or in a covered pot with 1 3/4 cups water: bring to a boil, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the beef into strips if it isn't already thin. Toss it with the flour, 1/4 tsp of the salt and the black pepper.
Cut the onions into thin strips, slice the mushrooms and mince the garlic.

Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add half the beef and cook for 1 minute, until it's no longer pink on the outside. Transfer it to a bowl and cook the second half the same way.
Melt the butter in the same pot over medium heat. Add the onions and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and golden at the edges.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until the paste darkens.
Pour in the red wine and scrape up the browned bits. Boil for 2 minutes, until it has reduced by half.
Add the Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, ketchup and brown sugar and stir. Add the tomato juice, the demi-glace and the bay leaf, then the mushrooms.
Return the beef and any juices in the bowl to the pot. Bring it to a boil and skim off any foam from the top with a spoon.
Turn the heat to low, cover and simmer for 15 minutes. Take out the bay leaf.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Just One Cookbook (the lead) makes a full homemade demi-glace, then sears sliced ribeye, softens onions in butter, cooks down tomato paste and red wine, adds Worcestershire, soy, ketchup, sugar and tomato juice, and simmers 15 minutes. RecipeTin Japan sears floured beef and uses a store-bought demi-glace with ketchup, Worcestershire, red wine, soy and brown sugar in a 30 minute version; Japanese Cooking 101 builds a brown roux instead. This version keeps the lead's method and sauce but uses a can of store-bought demi-glace (the lead's homemade one takes almost 3 hours) at half the lead's amount, and halves the tomato juice, so the sauce is slightly looser. RecipeTin Japan and Japanese Cooking 101 do not show a usable rating (1 vote); the lead's rating is from its visible '4.75 from 51 votes' line.
